findings.finding: pair_kernel_2.5 is positively associated with the high-versus-low integrated endpoint (z=0.631, 95% CI 0.495 to 0.758, q=2.19e-5), with positive batch fraction 1.0 and score correlation 0.213. This is an observed association, not a causal design rule.

pair_kernel_7.0 has the opposite association (z=-0.485, 95% CI -0.617 to -0.357, q=1.46e-4; positive batch fraction 0). Together with the positive 1.5–3.5 kernels, this argues against assuming that larger pair distance scales are uniformly favorable.

shape_yy is negatively associated with the integrated endpoint (z=-0.513, 95% CI -0.620 to -0.424, q=1.49e-5; positive batch fraction 0). Its last-minus-first time delta is small and positive (0.148), so the endpoint contrast does not establish a temporal trend.

landmark_00_occupancy3 has a positive endpoint association (z=0.545, 95% CI 0.393 to 0.699, q=2.35e-4; positive batch fraction 1.0); the supplied increment estimate is also positive but weaker after correction (q=0.081).

landmark_00_softmin has a negative success-versus-failure integrated rate contrast (z=-4.91, 95% CI -6.85 to -2.62, q=0.046; positive batch fraction 0.071). This differs from the positive landmark_00 occupancy3 association and cautions against treating nearby landmark summaries as interchangeable.

landmark_00_soft_mass is positively associated with regional enrichment (z=0.639, 95% CI 0.492 to 0.791, q=1.88e-4; positive batch fraction 1.0), an exploratory regional signal in the supplied selected evidence.

directions: Prioritize a controlled comparison of the allowed pair-kernel/contact scales, checking whether moderate-distance contact rewards retain the positive endpoint association while the 7.0-scale behavior remains unfavorable; interpret this as a hypothesis to test, not as a physical affinity result.

Test modest contact_weight settings (0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5) against the current setting and report endpoint, increment, and regional outcomes separately, since landmark occupancy, softmin, and soft_mass signals differ.

Run a small native_rms_ratio sweep (0.1, 0.2, 0.33) with otherwise fixed settings to see whether endpoint gains persist under tighter or looser native-geometry restraint; the current evidence does not identify a causal optimum.

For promising settings, compare time_ramp_power values (0, 1, 2) and require replicated endpoint outcomes before interpreting any time-dependent effect; the supplied last-minus-first deltas are feature-specific and are not a general temporal trend estimate.
limitations: The supplied tables are a compressed, exploratory selection of strongest and weakest q-values, not a complete enrichment analysis; unshown results and selection effects limit inference.
Associations across endpoint, increment, regional, and survival summaries are not causal effects of steering parameters, and correlated features should not be treated as independent confirmation.
The structure record describes the original bound ligand and receptor only, has no affinity labels, and cannot establish generated-Steer geometry or predict binding affinity.
No complete temporal analysis is supplied; isolated last-minus-first feature deltas do not support a broad selection-survival or temporal-trend claim.
